sensitivity: At $4,511,476 cost, $1 million/$100 thousand per 10 requires 45.11476/451.1476 net USA QALYs. With q=15 and g=.9, that is 3.34183/33.41834 fully additional discounted deaths prevented, compared with central .03438 before QALY conversion.
Price scales inversely with each positive multiplicative input. A political contribution of zero or complete donor replacement eliminates quantified benefit.
Using OSHA's 14-fold undercount alone instead of 3 improves the central price by 14/3, not enough to reach $1 million per 10. The favorable result requires multiple favorable assumptions together.

Any all-population harm above .51573 QALYs erases the central partial benefit. Nonfatal benefits and other pathways might add value, but are not established offsets.
Implementation delay matters: shifting the same stream five years later reduces it by 1/1.03^5. A paper rule without protection is zero, regardless of advocacy success.

what: Earthjustice provides free environmental legal representation alongside policy, scientific and public-information work.
Its portfolio includes clean air and water, toxic chemicals, energy, climate, wildlife and public lands across and beyond the United States.
A partial model of additional national soot-standard implementation gives about $35 million per 10 USA QALYs, with a favorable scenario around $279,000 and zero/harm possible.
strengths: A large specialist legal team can make binding public-health duties enforceable when agencies fail to act.
Current court records provide concrete evidence of implementation work rather than only claimed campaign victories.
Primary regulatory models and epidemiology connect cleaner air to clinical outcomes, allowing a numerical partial estimate.
reservations: Most recipient pathways remain unpriced, so the partial number is not an overall ranking.
Recent court victories already belong in the counterfactual; a new donor cannot claim the entire regulation.
Other litigators, state governments, reserves and existing gifts may replace the marginal contribution.

sections.what:
Earthjustice, EIN 94-1730465, supplies legal representation without charging public-interest clients. Litigation is supported by policy and public information; work spans health, energy and climate, public lands and wildlife. The ordinary recipient scope includes all these activities, not just the clean-air case modeled below. [Portfolio](https://earthjustice.org/feature/trump-environment-lawsuits)

The current financial report says staffing reached 600 and describes accelerated staffing growth. This indicates organizational capacity and demand, not 600 health-producing positions. Earthjustice Action is a separate 501(c)(4); the audit describes a reimbursement agreement, not consolidated inclusion of that organization's political work. [Financial report](https://earthjustice.org/about/financial-statements) [Audit](https://earthjustice.org/document/2025-audited-financials)
sections.monitoring:
The July 17, 2026 district-court order requires EPA to promulgate final PM2.5 area designations by February 6, 2027 and retains jurisdiction. It follows June's ruling upholding the strengthened standard. The order is a real implementation milestone, but designation is not attainment or a measured reduction in deaths. [Actual order](https://earthjustice.org/document/ruling-court-orders-epa-to-implement-national-soot-standard) [June result](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/court-upholds-life-saving-national-soot-air-quality-standard)

Earthjustice, Clean Air Task Force and Southern Environmental Law Center represented coalition groups, while state/local plaintiffs brought parallel claims. Future monitoring should distinguish designation, enforceable plans, actual controls and exposure changes; investigate which would be delayed without added legal capacity. [Counsel and partners](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/court-orders-epa-to-implement-national-soot-standard)

The active MATS case challenges repeal of 2024 amendments. It does not justify credit for all health gains from the original 2012 standards. The 2026 repeal and current legal challenge are separate from already-achieved historic reductions. [Challenge](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/coalition-sues-trump-epa-over-illegal-repeal-of-mercury-and-air-toxics-standards) [EPA status](https://www.epa.gov/stationary-sources-air-pollution/mercury-and-air-toxics-standards)
sections.qualitative:
The PM pathway has strong evidence beyond policy outputs. Wu and colleagues analyzed 68.5 million Medicare enrollees with five approaches and found broadly consistent mortality effects. Causal interpretation still requires confounding assumptions; predicted residential exposure has measurement error. This supports a causal health mechanism, not a measured Earthjustice effect. [Original study](https://xiaowu.io/publication/wu2020evaluating/wu2020evaluating.pdf)

EPA's native table provides alternative adult mortality estimates of 2,100 and 4,500 for identified controls under the revised annual standard in 2032. They must not be added. The model uses their midpoint as a judgment, then applies a transport haircut. It excludes infant and nonfatal outcomes, including asthma, to avoid case/utility overlap. Mortality occurs with a cessation lag; the QALY assumption includes that timing. [RIA, Table 5-5 and methods](https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2024-02/naaqs_pm_reconsideration_ria_final.pdf)

Habitat, climate and legal-access benefits may be important independently of USA health. They are not converted from acres, tonnes, case counts or economic damages. Litigation can also delay projects with benefits; implementation costs or energy access may harm health. No empirical estimate of those offsets was recovered, so zero and adverse scenarios remain.
sections.cost:
Audited full recipient expense is $183,685,874 for FY 2025, $165,760,409 for FY 2024 and $158,385,625 for FY 2023; the comparable mean is $169,277,303. Fiscal years end June 30. Latest expense includes $16,809,973 of donated legal and public-information services; these are retained as resources, not mistaken for cash spending. [FY 2025 audit](https://earthjustice.org/document/2025-audited-financials) [FY 2024 audit](https://earthjustice.org/document/2024-audited-financials)

Two annual budgets cost $367.4 million. The partial PM model produces 103.64 expected USA QALYs centrally, approximately $35.4 million per 10. The favorable joint scenario produces about 13,176 QALYs and costs about $279,000 per 10; a low-influence scenario is vastly worse. This is a partial pathway estimate, not a total recipient effectiveness claim or a guaranteed lower bound.

The model counts one conditional full-equivalent year of additional exposure protection at 2032 scale, with only a 10% incremental coalition probability, a 20% Earthjustice contribution and 50% funding additionality. It gives no new credit for the already-issued court order. Public regulators and pollution sources bear substantial implementation costs outside the recipient denominator; those resources are not free.
sections.funding:
The audit reports $56,995,368 of financial assets available for general expenditure within one year and a $201,282,311 board-designated reserve. The latter can be redesignated and is distinct from donor-restricted endowment assets. Those reserves support long-term legal obligations, but they also make complete next-dollar additionality implausible without a specific work plan. [Liquidity and reserve notes](https://earthjustice.org/document/2025-audited-financials)

FY 2025 revenue was $207,196,608 and net assets rose $23,510,734. Court-awarded fees and costs contributed $5,787,062; these can recycle resources after successful cases, but are not assured. The marginal funding question is whether support expands otherwise-unfunded legal work or mainly replenishes reserves. The staffing-growth statement is promising capacity evidence, not a quantified funding gap. [Current plans](https://earthjustice.org/about/financial-statements)

model.costScope: Two years of full FY 2025 audited recipient resources, including all programs, administration, fundraising and donated services. Separate c4 excluded. Regulatory agency and corporate compliance spending disclosed but not included in recipient cost.
model.geographicAttribution: Only domestic resident health in the EPA PM pathway is quantified, so g=1 by model scope. No overseas, territorial, biodiversity or global climate health credit is included. This is not an organization-wide USA allocation.
model.formula: C=2*183685874. Y(L,start)=sum(i=0..L-1)1/1.03^(start+i). Q_USA=Q_all=D*m*q*Y*p*a*b-H. D=(2100+4500)/2=3300 central; the two EPA mortality studies are alternatives, not additive. q is discounted lifetime health per death including cessation lag to the exposure year; Y discounts exposure years to2026. Price=10*C/Q_USA when positive.
model.counterfactual: Current 9µg/m3 standard, June 2026 defense victory and July 2026 designation order remain in baseline. L is the extra full-equivalent exposure protection secured by future implementation work, not all protection under the rule. p is coalition incremental chance of achieving that addition, with existing statutory duties and state/local litigation continuing.
model.attribution: Earthjustice is one of several important legal contributors. a=.2 subjective share of incremental coalition contribution, not share of all rule benefits. b=.5 discounts reserves, existing support, fee recovery and replacement gifts. A successful future case does not establish these values retrospectively.
model.uncertainty: Very-low-confidence partial expected-value assessment. Clinical mechanism is stronger than marginal policy attribution. The midpoint of two regulatory forecasts is judgment, not a posterior estimate; broad scenarios are not confidence intervals. Remaining recipient pathways can add benefits or harms, precluding a whole-recipient ranking from this number.
model.nativeOutcomes: Legally effective implementation, additional emissions/exposure reductions, full-equivalent protected exposure years, adult deaths prevented and discounted lifetime QALYs. Court orders, case counts, acres and tonnes are not themselves QALYs.

inputs.name: C
inputs.unit: USD, two annual full recipient budgets
inputs.rationale: Judgment extrapolation to two years at the observed annual recipient expense: 2×FY 2025 audited expense. Two-year support horizon is judgment; donated services included.

inputs.name: D
inputs.unit: modeled adult deaths avoided per 2032-equivalent protected year
inputs.rationale: Midpoint of alternative EPA 2100 and 4500 estimates, not their sum or a pooled clinical estimate. Baseline assumes current 12/35 standard; identified controls for revised 9/35, not all possible attainment benefits.

inputs.name: m
inputs.rationale: Allows uncertain composition, adherence, changing emissions and residual confounding; .3–1 scenarios. Not an EPA parameter.

inputs.name: q
inputs.unit: QALYs per avoided adult death, discounted to exposure year
inputs.rationale: Composite of remaining survival, health quality, competing mortality and cessation lag. Broad 1–10 range; not EPA VSL divided by a QALY price. An older-adult dominated benefit cannot be valued as a young person's full lifespan.

inputs.name: L
inputs.unit: full-equivalent years of pollution protection conditional on incremental success
inputs.rationale: One year of avoided delay or equivalent retained exposure reduction; favorable 3. Does not count an indefinite standard or July 2026 victory again.

inputs.name: start
inputs.unit: years from 2026 to first modeled exposure year
inputs.rationale: 2032 reference-year controls; later timing tested. Native benefits are not observed 2026 outcomes.

inputs.name: r
inputs.rationale: Y discounts exposure timing. q already includes within-person lifetime and cessation-lag discounting.

inputs.name: p
inputs.unit: incremental coalition probability of securing protection beyond baseline
inputs.rationale: Subjective 10-percentage-point implementation contribution, not raw court win probability. Existing binding order and legal duties sharply constrain available additional credit.

inputs.name: a
inputs.unit: Earthjustice share of incremental coalition contribution
inputs.rationale: Counsel with important technical/client capacity, but state/local plaintiffs, CATF, SELC and other groups can substitute. .05–.5 scenarios; no equal division or sole credit.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: Growth plans support capacity use, but reserve funding and replacement gifts can preserve existing commitments. .1–.8 scenarios; no measured marginal staffing-to-outcome response.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: USA share of this quantified domestic branch
inputs.rationale: The model intentionally includes only US resident effects in EPA domestic analysis. This is not a claim that all Earthjustice work or all global benefits are domestic.

inputs.name: H
inputs.rationale: Provisional zero, with explicit net-harm case. Energy-cost/access effects, implementation displacement and litigation downside not measured.

sensitivity: At $367,371,748 cost, $1 million/$100 thousand per 10 requires 3673.71748/36737.1748 net USA QALYs, versus 103.63868 centrally.

With q=5 and other central values, the $1 million threshold requires about 35.45 times the central product of protected years and incremental contribution. One favorable parameter alone need not achieve it.
Using only the 2100 or 4500 mortality alternatives changes central health by 2100/3300 or 4500/3300. These are not confidence bounds; uncertainty also includes model transport and exposure changes.

Using the three-year mean reduces cost about 7.8%. Excluding all donated services from latest expense reduces cost 9.15%, but omits real legal resources and public-service advertising; neither adjustment solves marginal attribution.
A delay from 2032 to 2036 reduces benefits by 1/1.03^4. q includes post-exposure cessation lag; do not count all modeled deaths as immediate.
All-population harm above 103.63868 QALYs erases the central partial benefit. Zero future implementation effect gives no finite positive price.
A portfolio sum must de-duplicate PM effects of MATS, power-plant, permitting and ambient-standard cases before adding them. Historic successes are not new-donation yield.

what: CBE combines community organizing, scientific research and litigation to reduce pollution in California communities.
Its work includes Exide cleanup and refinery disputes in Los Angeles, alongside substantial Bay Area and statewide activity.
A judgment-based partial-health central estimate is about $75.5 million per 10 LA/Orange QALYs; it is not an observed return or a donor-ready recommendation.
strengths: Current primary documents identify concrete cleanup barriers, including access to multi-family properties.
Legal, scientific and resident knowledge can complement government cleanup capacity.
Original financial returns identify the full recipient cost rather than only a selected campaign budget.
reservations: Policy probability, exposed population, dose reduction and marginal funding response are judgment inputs, with no verified next-dollar work plan; zero or harm remains possible.
The effect of remaining soil remediation on local blood lead and clinical outcomes is not measured here.
Statewide activity and coalition overlap prevent allocating all recipient benefits to Los Angeles.

sections.what:
CBE, EIN 94-2998086, operates in Southeast Los Angeles and Wilmington as well as East Oakland and Richmond. Ordinary support funds organizing, science, legal work, education and statewide initiatives. Its current support page reports more than 10,000 community members, 530 meetings annually and over 70 staff; these are scale claims, not health outcomes. The donation page explicitly identifies the recipient and EIN. [Recipient and operations](https://www.cbecal.org/donate/)

The current refinery portfolio includes Long Beach storage expansion, Paramount/Altair conversion, national hydrogen-fluoride regulation and statewide fuel-policy litigation. Several cases involve Earthjustice, East Yard or other counsel; activity and shared representation do not identify a sole causal owner. [Current cases](https://www.cbecal.org/initiative/refineries/)

In August 2026 CBE launched a two-year, ten-organization statewide climate-adaptation cohort supported by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. That is current implementation capacity, but the announcement does not identify additional cooling/smoke protection, utilization or clinical effects. Existing foundation support belongs in the funding counterfactual. [CACHE launch](https://www.cbecal.org/news/post/10-community-led-orgs-launch-statewide-climate-adaptation-efforts/)
sections.monitoring:
CBE's March 2026 letter recognizes progress on Exide cleanup while requesting better owner participation, retrospective sampling and state/federal contingency planning. It also identifies delayed technical-assistance grants and problems at other contaminated sites. These are plausible actionable bottlenecks, but the letter does not count additional homes cleaned because of CBE or report residents' health changes. [Current intervention](https://www.cbecal.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/CBEs-Comment-Letter-on-the-Board-of-Environmental-Safety-Evaluation-of-DTSC.pdf)

The March legislative briefing says over 6,000 high-priority properties had been cleaned by end-2025 and describes remaining contaminated parcels and proposed new funding. It requests $70 million in each of two fiscal years, yet separately describes $70 million for about 1,000 parcels. That internal cost/scope ambiguity means neither $70,000 nor $140,000 is presented as a verified marginal cleanup price. The proposal is not treated as enacted funding. [Primary budget record, p. 36](https://sbud.senate.ca.gov/system/files/2026-03/agenda-mar19-calepa-3.16.pdf)

Useful monitoring would link otherwise-inaccessible households to actual access, completed remediation, sustained environmental and blood-lead changes, age-specific exposure duration and clinical outcomes. Measure what happens later without the additional advocacy, not only treatment versus no cleanup ever.
sections.qualitative:
The mechanism is biologically credible but heterogeneous. A Boston randomized trial of 152 young children with much higher baseline soil lead found roughly 1.5–1.9 micrograms/dL greater blood-lead declines from soil abatement than comparison interventions. Its median baseline soil concentration was 2,075 ppm; that is not directly portable to the lower-concentration Exide parcels now being considered. [Original trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/405094)

The later HOME randomized trial enrolled 355 pregnancies and followed children through age eight. It reduced dust lead but found no statistically significant overall blood-lead reduction and no substantive neurobehavioral improvement; a subgroup had greater exposure reduction. This is not evidence that all remediation fails, but it makes a universal QALY-per-house assumption unsafe. Neither soil ppm nor an IQ/earnings estimate is silently converted to QALYs. [Original HOME trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/2696978)

The refinery air pathway is more directly modelable clinically: AQMD's draft assessment reports PM-related deaths and morbidity, rather than only tonnes or monetized benefits. However, Rule 1109.1 was adopted in 2021, with implementation scheduled over subsequent years. The historical total is not a new donor's impact. No current CBE-specific change to remaining compliance, associated emissions or LA/Orange exposure was established. [Native table](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/rule-book/Proposed-Rules/1109.1/1109-1-draft-socioeconomic-impact-assessment-090721-merged.pdf?sfvrsn=10) [Adoption](https://www.aqmd.gov/home/research/pubs-docs-reports/newsletters/jan-feb-2022/refinery-rule)

Community voice, accountability and environmental justice can matter independently of health. Cleanup can also create dust, displacement or exported waste burdens. These are not presumed zero merely because clinical quantification is absent.

A more geographically analogous smelter-cleanup study in Omaha found lower elevated blood-lead odds in several models, but no intervention association in its fully adjusted difference-in-differences model. The authors caution that remediation and measurement timing were highly correlated. This strengthens the case for local longitudinal measurement rather than selecting only a favorable before/after result. [Original researchers' summary](https://assessments.epa.gov/risk/document/&deid=354467)
sections.cost:
Original returns report full recipient expenses of $4,803,145 (2022), $6,001,139 (2023) and $7,882,417 (2024); the mean is $6,228,900.33. No reported separately netted event/inventory costs require restoration. [Original 2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/942998086/202523219349326347/full)

The central model charges five full budgets at the latest annual expense, not only a selected campaign cost. Technical/legal and organizing capacity changes the probability of additional enforceable refinery/fuel-related emissions controls beyond existing permits and Rule 1109.1. Current World Oil and Paramount disputes establish a live mechanism, not the assumed probability or PM reduction. HF accident prevention, soil lead, Bay Area activity and non-health justice value are not converted to PM mortality.

Conditional on an additional policy increment, 250,000 older residents experience 0.3 micrograms/m³ less annual ambient PM2.5. A 8% recipient-specific increase in that policy probability over the five-year effort and 35% marginal funding response are judgments, not measured attribution. The funding response allows for reserves and replacement gifts; coalition contribution is already inside the probability change and is not discounted twice. The assumed exposed cohort is alive at implementation, three years after model start.

Using the external HR 1.06 per 10 micrograms/m³, a 0.7 log-risk transport factor, annual baseline mortality hazard 0.035 and survivor utility 0.75, integrate competing all-cause survival curves for ten years and discount at 3%. Half the modeled effect is durable within that window; half is three-year acceleration of an otherwise identical policy. Acceleration retains only the finite survival difference versus delayed implementation. No lifetime QALYs are appended. All inputs beyond the external study estimate and financial accounts are judgments. [External clinical study](https://xiaowu.io/publication/wu2020evaluating/wu2020evaluating.pdf)

The $10,000 normalization yields 0.0013250 local QALYs and $75,471,532 per 10. Favorable and poor joint scenarios give $516,735 and $3,795,077,413,953 per 10; they are sensitivity cases, not confidence limits. Zero and net-harm cases have no finite beneficial price. This is a partial-health estimate: omitted pathways have zero net central contribution by judgment, not proven absence of benefit or harm. Public implementation, regulated-facility, volunteer and partner resources are additional unpriced social costs; this is not an all-resource societal cost-effectiveness estimate.
sections.funding:
The 2024 return reports revenue of $8,062,410, year-end cash of $5,989,690 and unrestricted net assets of $5,964,296. These balances do not prove that every asset is freely deployable today, but they weaken an assumption of immediate one-for-one expansion from an additional gift. Expense grew about 31% from 2023, while the return records 83 employees during the year; headcount is not full-time equivalents. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/942998086/202523219349326347/full)

A useful next-dollar case would specify otherwise-unfunded organizers or technical/legal capacity, the affected cleanup queue or enforceable emissions change, and why reserves, agency outreach, other funders or partner groups would not replace it. Current broad fundraising claims do not provide that marginal work plan. [Support page](https://www.cbecal.org/donate/) The current jobs page lists no available positions; that is a website observation, not proof that the organization lacks useful work or cannot expand. [Current vacancies](https://www.cbecal.org/get-involved/jobs/)

model.costScope: Five full latest-year gross reported recipient budgets, across all programs and support, normalized linearly to a $10,000 ordinary gift. No policy-only cost carveout. External social resources unpriced.
model.geographicAttribution: Only health within Los Angeles and Orange counties (FIPS 06037, 06059) is counted. The 250,000 older adults are an analyst-selected conditional exposure cohort, not an office-count allocation or observed participant total. Riverside and San Bernardino outcomes are excluded. allPopulationQalys equals local quantified branch only, not an assumption that the whole portfolio is local.
model.formula: h1=h0*exp(-ln(HR)/10*transport*pm); rho=ln(1.03); F(a,t)=(1-exp(-a*t))/a. qD=u*(F(h1+rho,T)-F(h0+rho,T)). a=min(A,T). qT=u*(F(h1+rho,a)-F(h0+rho,a)+(1-exp(-(h0-h1)*a))*(exp(-(h1+rho)*a)-exp(-(h1+rho)*T))/(h1+rho)). q=(f*qD+(1-f)*qT)/1.03^L. Qgift=10000/(E*Y)*b*(p*N*q-harm). Price=100000/Qgift if positive. N is cohort alive at implementation; no extra survival-to-implementation multiplier. Costs are constant-real full budgets; no cost discount haircut.
model.counterfactual: Already-completed properties, adopted air rules, public cleanup appropriations and work by regulators, residents and partner organizations continue without the marginal support. Acceleration must count only the exposure interval gained, not lifetime no-cleanup benefit. Technical/legal and organizing capacity changes the probability of additional enforceable refinery/fuel-related emissions controls beyond existing permits and Rule 1109.1. Current World Oil and Paramount disputes establish a live mechanism, not the assumed probability or PM reduction. HF accident prevention, soil lead, Bay Area activity and non-health justice value are not converted to PM mortality.
model.attribution: p is the incremental recipient-specific probability effect of a five-year whole-organization effort versus partner/regulator action without it. b models donation-sensitive capacity after replacement funding, distinct from coalition p. Local linear extrapolation to a small gift is judgment and can fail at lumpy capacity thresholds.
model.uncertainty: Explicit judgment central, not identified causal charity effectiveness. Wide scenarios include clinical-null, no-policy-effect and harm. This is not a complete portfolio estimate or a reason to override donor diligence.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional annual ambient PM2.5 exposure reduction among an explicitly modeled older cohort; finite discounted all-cause survival differences, without adding overlapping mortality/morbidity or lead/IQ units.

what: East Yard organizes residents around pollution, transportation, housing stability, youth leadership and local food systems in eastern and southern Los Angeles County.
Its community-academic lead study helped change cleanup oversight; current work also addresses port emissions and a proposed resilience hub.
A conditional air-implementation estimate prices additional health at full recipient cost, with explicit subjective assumptions; it is not a complete portfolio return.
strengths: Original research documents a specific cleanup failure and subsequent oversight changes.

sections.what:
East Yard, EIN 46-5685097, is a community-based environmental justice organization. Its membership areas include East LA, Boyle Heights, Long Beach and Southeast LA cities, all within LA County. It also participates in statewide and regional coalitions, so its total health footprint is not automatically 100% within the LA+Orange boundary. [Membership geography](https://eycej.org/index.php/about/membership/)

The recipient includes tenant organizing, youth and leadership work, community research, composting, gardening and pollution advocacy. La Cosecha's garden builds and produce exchange may support well-being; its traditional-remedy workshops are cultural/educational activities, not assigned clinical efficacy or QALYs. [Programs](https://eycej.org/index.php/la-cosecha-colectiva/)

The official donation page links a Raisely campaign, but the fetched payment page did not expose a verifiable legal payee, so no donation button is asserted here. [Official route](https://eycej.org/index.php/donate/)
sections.monitoring:
The 2026 Get the Lead Out paper reports 1,128 soil samples from 373 properties, including 143 previously remediated homes. Sampling found 105 of those homes had at least one sample above 80 ppm. Recruitment used meetings, social media and outreach, with selected downwind neighborhoods prioritized; it was not a representative randomized audit. The study did not compare directly with original samples because methods differed, and cannot distinguish inadequate initial removal from recontamination on every property. [Original study and methods](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13085797/)

Importantly, the authors describe concrete subsequent changes: verification sampling in new contracts, a state-funded third-party monitor and expanded blood-lead testing access. Verification results were still forthcoming. These are credible intermediate outcomes, not proof of health effect or sole EYCEJ causation. Already-established oversight cannot be credited afresh to new support. [Study implementation discussion](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13085797/)

The older campaign page still describes waiting for an I-710 final EIR and other historic statuses; it is used to identify scope, not to date current milestones. Current agency documents show the ports agreement is already effective. [Campaign scope](https://eycej.org/index.php/campaigns/) [Current status](https://www.aqmd.gov/home/air-quality/air-quality-management-plans/air-quality-mgt-plan/facility-based-mobile-source-measures/comm-ports-wkng-grp/potential-cooperative-agreement-with-the-ports-of-long-beach-and-los-angeles)

A July 2026 suit names East Yard as a plaintiff in the Barstow International Gateway challenge. This is concrete current litigation, but the rail facility is in San Bernardino County, outside this edition. Potential effects along the LA–Barstow route require geographically resolved net traffic and emissions, not assigning all alleged project emissions to LA residents. [Counsel's case announcement](https://earthjustice.org/press/2026/lawsuit-challenges-approval-of-nations-largest-rail-facility-in-california)
sections.qualitative:
Lead remediation is a plausible health mechanism, but a reduction in soil concentration is not itself a QALY. The Boston randomized trial found blood-lead improvement at high baseline soil contamination; the later HOME trial found no significant overall blood-lead effect or substantive neurobehavioral improvement. These do not invalidate cleanup, but they require local exposure, age and persistence inputs before assigning a per-house clinical yield. The original trials were first reviewed in the CBE research interval and reused here, with EYCEJ-specific interpretation separately timed. [Boston trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/405094) [HOME trial](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapediatrics/fullarticle/2696978)

Air pollution has a better-established mortality bridge: a large Medicare study found broadly consistent PM2.5 effects across several causal-inference approaches, subject to confounding and exposure-measurement assumptions. The missing link here is not whether polluted air can harm people, but the additional emissions and exposure changes that EYCEJ's marginal work would produce. [Original PM study](https://xiaowu.io/publication/wu2020evaluating/wu2020evaluating.pdf)

The September 10, 2026 port addendum adds ship and zero-emission truck incentives plus $40 million total off-port charging/fueling funding. Truck-program approval is due February 28, 2027, with possible extensions. Participation goals and quantified benefits remain to be developed; the agreement explicitly acknowledges uptake is beyond the ports' control. The off-port fund covers the South Coast basin, not just LA+Orange. [Actual addendum](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/ports-ca/addendum-to-ports-ca_final-approved-sept-2026.pdf?sfvrsn=a4db637e_2)

East Yard was part of the coalition contesting the earlier port proposal and joined the May 2026 demand for refinery monitoring during decommissioning. These establish active roles; neither a letter nor a monitor establishes avoided exposure without an ensuing action. Coalition credit must not be duplicated across EYCEJ, CBE, CCA, Earthjustice and others. [Port coalition](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/planning/fbmsm-docs/2025-10-01-final-scaqmd-gov-board-ltr-re-draft-cooperative-agreement.pdf?sfvrsn=eaaa6c7e_2) [Monitoring coalition](https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/rule-book/proposed-rules/rule-1180-and-1180.1/2026/comment-letters/2026-05-11-coalition.pdf?sfvrsn=cc32677e_2)

The new central scenario assumes a three-year organizing effort has a 20% chance of improving implementation beyond adopted commitments enough to reduce PM2.5 by 0.1 microgram per cubic meter for 100,000 older adults for five years. Neither that exposure footprint nor the success probability is measured or source-calibrated. EYCEJ receives 10% of coalition contribution and a 25% marginal funding response. This is a transparent judgment scenario, not an agency forecast. A closed-cohort survival integral follows the cohort for ten years, with mortality hazard returning to baseline after year five and no benefit after year ten. This avoids repeated lifetime credits for the same people. Lead cleanup, housing, gardens and the proposed hub remain unpriced.
sections.cost:
Full 2024 recipient cost is $1,562,510: reported functional expense of $1,539,414 plus $23,096 of event costs netted against revenue. The functional split is $1,256,380 program, $195,000 administration and $88,034 fundraising. Comparable 2023 and amended 2022 totals are $1,118,780 and $1,030,737, with no reported netted event/inventory adjustments; the three-year mean is $1,237,342. These are original accrual returns; an independent audit is indicated in the latest return but was not recovered. [2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202512769349301586/full) [2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202433179349305163/full) [2022](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202421919349301957/full)

At the latest annual cost, $100,000 per 10 LA QALYs requires 156.251 net additional QALYs; $1 million per 10 requires 15.6251. For an air-mortality pathway, an illustrative 5 discounted QALYs per death would require 31.25 or 3.13 expected additional LA deaths avoided, after all coalition and funding adjustments. This is a decision threshold, not a claim that East Yard achieves those totals.

The conditional air component uses three annual full recipient budgets, $4,687,530. It yields 0.254947 LA QALY, about $183.86 million per 10. A favorable joint case is about $451,475 per 10; a weak case exceeds $13 trillion per 10. These are judgment stress cases, not confidence limits.

The scenario assumes better use of already-committed implementation resources. Any additional vehicles, chargers, monitoring or operating resources must be added for a social-cost price; the $40 million already committed is not created by a new gift. Hub capital and benefits are excluded.
sections.funding:
The 2024 return reports $4,238,201 cash, $3,651,369 other investments and $7,318,249 unrestricted net assets, compared with about $1.56 million annual full cost. These assets may be designated or intended for long-term commitments; unrestricted accounting is not evidence of immediate availability. Nevertheless, assuming every additional dollar expands current operations would be weak. [Original balance sheet](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/465685097/202512769349301586/full)

The June 2026 transition announcement specifically seeks capital-campaign support to replace a freight-focused warehouse with a community resilience hub. It provides no acquisition price, funding gap, operating plan or number of protected heat/smoke-exposure hours. The July update identifies Laura Cortez as current executive director as Taylor Thomas transitions out; old co-director listings are not used as current governance evidence. [Current transition and capital plan](https://eycej.org/index.php/blog/blog/)

East Yard has concrete local accountability evidence, but this highly assumption-sensitive component does not establish a whole-portfolio health-cost-effectiveness recommendation. The decisive diligence is a marginal operating/capital plan tied to verified extra exposure protection, with public funding and partner substitution explicitly separated. Clean Energy Group's historical 2021 award supported microgrid/community-solar capacity and advocacy; it does not establish that the proposed 2026 hub is operating or that its capital gap is known. [Original funder record](https://www.cleanegroup.org/initiatives/resilient-power-leadership-initiative/awards/)

what: VACF provides culturally accessible health education, screening, navigation and support, primarily in Orange County.
Its current legal name is Vital Access Care Foundation, reflecting a wider portfolio than cancer alone.
The numerical scenario prices only a hepatitis-care component against all recipient expenses, not the return from its entire portfolio.
strengths: Original organization-linked research documents a high hepatitis B burden in its historical screening population.
Language-access navigation offers a concrete route from testing to care for underserved residents.
Original accounts and current program descriptions establish a real, expanding recipient rather than an isolated screening campaign.
reservations: The current screening mix, unique HBV participants and completed-care cascade are not published.
The central estimate is a conditional partial-health scenario; most portfolio benefits remain unpriced.
Large recent surpluses and unrestricted reserves weaken the case that the next ordinary gift immediately expands services.

sections.what: The [current program portfolio](https://www.vacf.org/programs) includes cancer screening and support, public-benefit navigation, food assistance, research participation and community workforce development. The [organization describes an Orange County service focus](https://www.vacf.org/about), not an LA-city-only service. Its legal name in the [original 2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/912170415/202523219349307047/full) is Vital Access Care Foundation, with Vietnamese American Cancer Foundation in its mission description.
sections.monitoring: The 2024 return reports 2,499 combined screenings/vaccinations and 282 cancer patients assisted; these are outputs, not lives saved. The current website's 2025 impact heading links an image whose filename still says 2024; the image shows 3,750 screening/prevention activities. We use the dated return cohort, not that ambiguously labeled image, for numerical scale. VACF's [2019 HBV study](https://www.vacf.org/_files/ugd/dd68d6_5174bf64856744a4af4985d3f0c2c316.pdf) found 225 current infections among 2,508 participants but explicitly lacked information on completed necessary care. Improved monitoring would publish unique tests by disease, prior diagnosis, confirmatory results, referral completion and treatment/vaccination outcomes.
sections.qualitative: The [historical local study](https://www.vacf.org/_files/ugd/dd68d6_5174bf64856744a4af4985d3f0c2c316.pdf) documents bilingual education, mailed results and linkage efforts, supporting a plausible access mechanism. Its cross-sectional prevalence is not a causal treatment effect. The [HBV economic model](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6346293/) supplies a disease-progression bridge, not a VACF evaluation. We heavily reduce its applicability to older clients and unknown follow-through. Cancer support, food security, caregiver capacity and research may matter substantially but are not assigned arbitrary QALYs.
sections.cost: Whole-recipient 2024 Form 990 expenses were $2,205,208: $2,153,424 program, $49,846 management and $1,938 fundraising. Part VIII reports no separately netted fundraising expenses. Comparable Part IX expenses were $1,349,832 in 2023 and $1,038,000 in 2022 (confirmed directly in the original 2022 return, whose Part VIII reports zero event costs and no gaming, rental or inventory costs to restore); the three-year mean is $1,531,013.33. The central conditional hepatitis component is about $18.35 million per 10 LA-MSA QALYs, with deliberately wide positive scenarios and a zero-benefit case. This is not a complete portfolio ranking. Clinical treatment costs paid by insurers or partners are outside the donor-cost numerator.
sections.funding: The [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/912170415/202523219349307047/full) reports revenue of $3,252,848, a $1,047,640 surplus, $4,035,365 cash and $4,049,616 net assets without donor restrictions. Government grants are blank in Part VIII, which does not prove absence of publicly supported partner care. The [program page](https://www.vacf.org/programs) explicitly connects patients to Every Woman Counts and other assistance. An ordinary gift may support the entire expanded portfolio or reserves; no verified cash-only service queue was found. Funding responsiveness is therefore a judgment, not an observed grant-to-treatment conversion.

acceptance.evidence: docs/la-next-eight-acceptance.md

what: Maternal Mental Health NOW trains providers and supports parents facing perinatal mental-health challenges.
It became independent from Community Partners on July 1, 2025.
Our numerical scenario uses the full program operating budget and estimates training plus peer-support health effects, not the entire social and policy portfolio.
strengths: Provider training has a plausible multiplier through clinical practice, with randomized external health-outcome evidence.
Sana Sana supplies ongoing, culturally responsive local peer support rather than only a resource listing.
Primary reporting distinguishes unique clients from repeated interactions and describes reimbursement barriers.
reservations: The $1.17m denominator is a reported operating budget, not an audited current annual expense; the tiny standalone transition return cannot replace it.
Training attendance and confidence do not establish changed clinical practice, caseload or health effects.
Central benefits depend heavily on subjective transfer and funding assumptions; zero and adverse effects remain possible.

sections.what: The [current mission and model](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/about-us/) combine provider training, stigma reduction and access to care. [Sana Sana](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/sana/) offers ongoing peer contact and resource navigation for LA County parents. The [FY25 impact report](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/MMHN-Impact-Report-FY25.pdf) dates independence from Community Partners to July 1, 2025; today’s gift is not a gift to all of the former sponsor’s projects.
sections.monitoring: The [donation page](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/donate/) reports 800+ trainees and 150 warmline callers during 2024–25. We do not add 300 support-group participants to callers because overlap and attendance definitions are unresolved. The [December 2025 Sana Sana white paper](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/MMHN-whitepaper-Dec2025-1.pdf) distinguishes repeated interactions from unique clients, reports low survey response, and describes weekly 30–60-minute support. Its billing projections are not actual reimbursement. Provider confidence and non-random differences between home-visitor and clinic screening are not causal health outcomes.
sections.qualitative: The [PoNDER economic analysis](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6518383/) found a small adjusted six-month QALY gain from intensive UK health-visitor training in lower-risk postpartum women; uncertainty included no health gain. Our training model retains only 10% of that reference effect before further additionality and funding reductions. A [Canadian peer-support trial](https://www.bmj.com/content/338/bmj.a3064) found less probable depression at 12 weeks in high-risk women, but no significant difference at 24 weeks after referral of severe cases. It supports short-term benefit, not permanent remission. [LAMMHA’s funder report](https://www.chcf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CollaborativeCareModelImprovesMaternalMentalHealth.pdf) identifies MMHN as training coordinator within a larger clinical coalition; all clinical outcomes cannot be assigned to MMHN.
sections.cost: The [FY25 report](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/MMHN-Impact-Report-FY25.pdf) gives a $1.17m operating budget. The model uses that full-program planning scale, with $1.0m–$1.5m cost sensitivities, pending actual successor accounts. The [original FY2025 standalone 990-EZ](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/991790214/202600839349201225/full) has only $1,513 expenses and no payroll while the operational program remained sponsored; using that as the cost of its reported work would be wrong. No comparable three-year recipient expense mean is available. The central training/peer health component is about $26.58m per 10 LA-MSA QALYs. This is a conditional planning estimate, not a complete portfolio return or validated historical cost-effectiveness result.
sections.funding: The FY25 operating-budget graphic attributes 55% to foundations/corporate, 25% government, 15% earned income and 5% individuals. Public and philanthropic support already finances delivery. The [current LAMMHA page](https://ccalac.org/los-angeles-maternal-mental-health-access-lammha/) describes the 2022–26 coalition program, closed enrollment and clinic implementation grants; these belong in the baseline. The [Sana Sana paper](https://maternalmentalhealthnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/MMHN-whitepaper-Dec2025-1.pdf) examines prospective billing, not guaranteed revenue, and [DHCS](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal-peer-support-services/) confirms specialty-system peer support is a defined benefit rather than universal reimbursement for every peer interaction. Ordinary gifts may preserve uncovered capacity, replace other funding or fund administration; 50% marginal responsiveness is an explicit judgment. A post-transition budget, sponsor transfer reconciliation and cash runway would materially improve the estimate.

sensitivity: The positive low/high scenarios are stress tests, not calibrated probability quantiles; training caseload and clinical implementation dominate. Zero additional funding response yields zero benefit.

The original training Table 5 QALY difference is .002 with 95% CI−.001 to .004. Cost-saving probability is not a 99% probability of improved health; NHS cost savings are not subtracted from this donor numerator.

Training benefit ends at six-month follow-up for each modeled parent, with only one annual cohort. Peer benefit is .1 utility for 12 weeks per incremental probable-depression case; no persistence beyond 24 weeks assumed. The peer benefit area is a subjective scenario, not the trial's measured duration of improvement.

At the central $1.17m budget, $1m/10 requires 11.7 LA QALYs; $100k/10 requires 117. Central modeled component=.44021. With other factors fixed, training caseload would need about 835 lower-risk parents per effective trainee to approach $1m/10; do not treat that threshold as observed capacity.

Cost should be updated from reconciled current recipient accounts; $1,513 is not a cheaper valid scenario. Paid clinical follow-through is a necessary complementary resource and could materially raise societal costs.

sections.what:
UPI is the independent nonprofit Connie Rice Institute for Urban Peace, EIN 36-4816075. Its ordinary support funds training, technical assistance, regranting, community safety and justice reform, including work beyond Los Angeles. The official donation page identifies this recipient and EIN. No restricted Peacemakers-only gift is assumed. [Recipient](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/donate/)

LA Peacemakers braids $9.6 million of public and private support across 18 independent organizations during 2024–2026. Its first-year report covers February 2024–January 2025 and reports 1,027 new participants. These are observed operational counts, not 1,027 people whose lives were saved. [Year-one report](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/LA-Peacemakers-Y1-Report.pdf)
sections.monitoring:
The year-one report compares two successive six-month periods: fatal injuries fell from 54 to 47 and nonfatal injuries from 115 to 87. Changing exposure, reporting, seasonality and background violence could explain part or all of the difference. The counts concern coalition participants, not necessarily the 1,027 newly enrolled people used in this model. They are not used to calculate an observed treatment effect. [Internal evaluation](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/LA-Peacemakers-Y1-Report.pdf)

A newer progress report records over 1,500 cumulative new participants and support for 100 frontline and administrative positions. These are not all new full-time employees or an annual unique-client denominator. The subsequent February 2026 statement reports almost 2,000 cumulative enrollments. This supports continued activity but not an independently established clinical effect. [Progress report](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/LA-Peacemakers-Initiative-Progress-Report.pdf) [Current statement](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/homicides-drop-by-nearly-27-in-neighborhoods-most-impacted-by-violence-in-2025/)

The decisive next measurements are unique engaged clients, risk and person-time, services actually received, independently linked fatal/nonfatal outcomes, comparable untreated trajectories and otherwise-unfunded partner capacity.
sections.qualitative:
READI Chicago randomly offered intensive employment, cognitive-behavioral programming and support to high-risk men. The control group experienced about 11 shooting/homicide victimizations per 100 people over 20 months. The primary violence index was not significantly improved; overall victimizations were 12% lower, also not significant. The outreach-referred subgroup had a stronger 43% reduction. UPI's broader partner services are not READI, and selecting that subgroup as the UPI effect would overstate transportability. I therefore use an explicitly subjective 10% relative reduction, not a claimed experimental estimate for UPI. [Researchers' brief](https://crimelab.uchicago.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2023/08/READI-July-2023.pdf)

A 2026 Richmond synthetic-control study estimates a much larger citywide reduction, but its permutation inference was not significant, no California cities remained in the donor pool, and concurrent interventions limit attribution. Its 61% headline is not transported into this model. [Original study](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2853466)

A small Boston survivor study documents substantial pain, PTSD and functional limitations at 6–12 months. It supports nonfatal morbidity as important, but selection and absence of a utility estimate prevent treating it as a measured QALY loss. The model's 0.5 QALY per avoided nonfatal injury remains a broad clinical judgment. Death prevention receives 20 discounted QALYs, approximately 47 remaining years at utility 0.8 and 3% annual discounting; this is not an observed age-specific UPI life table. No arrest, dollar-of-crime-cost or community-event count is converted to health. [Survivor study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32530586/)
sections.cost:
The original FY2025 accrual return reports $8,897,684 of full recipient expenses: $7,075,093 program, $1,264,399 administration and $558,192 fundraising, including $3,625,415 in grants to domestic organizations. No event or inventory costs were reported netted against revenue. FY2024 operating expense is $5,293,277; a separate $100,000 leasehold disposal loss brings broader resource use to $5,393,277 but is excluded from the operating-expense comparison. FY2023 is $3,185,128. The three-year operating-expense mean is $5,792,030. The current model still uses full FY2025 recipient expense; no modeled benefit or current cost changes. [Latest return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/364816075/202630969349301208/full) [Comparative audit](https://docs.candid.org/efiles/9507579/c9e4bb9e-43f7-4903-bc14-803e25ab17f2.pdf)

Charging the full latest cost to 1,027 prospective annual participant-equivalents gives $8,664 per participant-equivalent before attribution. This is a full-cost normalization, not UPI's reported service price. With the explicit risk, effectiveness, health-value and funding assumptions below, the modeled branch generates 6.78 net additional LA QALYs, or about $13.1 million per 10. Positive joint scenarios span roughly $0.30 million to $11 billion per 10; they are stress tests, not confidence limits. Zero or harm has no finite beneficial price.

All non-LA work and unmodeled justice-reform activity remain in the denominator. Partner cofunding and public services outside UPI are real additional social resources, not included in the donor-cost denominator; their independent contribution is discounted through a. The omitted benefits and omitted harms mean this is not a mathematical lower bound.
sections.funding:
FY2025 revenue was $12,539,904, including $5,292,475 in government grants. Year-end cash was $6,898,638 and unrestricted net assets $6,213,733. These are historical balances, not verified uncommitted cash today. They caution against assuming every new dollar immediately creates a new service. [Original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/364816075/202630969349301208/full)

UPI's February 2026 statement says Peacemakers funding expires during 2026 without an identified replacement. This is a specific continuation opportunity, but not an independently verified remaining gap or renewal probability. A separate CalVIP coalition announcement describes $107 million in new statewide funding; it does not establish a UPI award. Central funding additionality b=0.5 balances a plausible cliff against reserves, renewed public funding and donor substitution. [UPI](https://www.urbanpeaceinstitute.org/homicides-drop-by-nearly-27-in-neighborhoods-most-impacted-by-violence-in-2025/) [CalVIP](https://giffords.org/press-release/2026/02/calvip-coalition-statement-on-107-million-in-new-funding-for-community-violence-intervention/)

The audit download indexed as FY2025 actually contains FY2024 statements plus a February 2026 corrective-action attachment. Its cover and activity table were visually checked; it is not used as a FY2025 audit. It describes contribution-recognition controls and planned improvements, but the period mismatch prevents attributing an apparent current finding solely from the index. Obtain the correctly matched current audit and evidence that the controls were implemented. [Filed audit package](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_audit/2025-06-GSAFAC-0000403801)

model.costScope: Full annual recipient resource expense, including regrants, administration, fundraising and non-LA work. Only a selected LA participant-health pathway is quantified; external partner/public resources are not misrepresented as UPI spending.
model.geographicAttribution: g=1 for the modeled LA Peacemakers participant branch within LA County. This is not a claim that all UPI activity or benefit is local; Orange residents qualify but no separate Orange benefit is invented. National training and statewide justice work remain unquantified.
model.formula: Q_LA=N*r*e*(f*qd+(1-f)*qn)*a*b*g-H; price=10*C/Q_LA when positive. C=8,897,684; N=1,027; r=.04; e=.10; f=.20; qd=20; qn=.5; a=.75; b=.5; g=1; H=0. One year of risk reduction per annual cohort; qd and qn include discounted downstream health from that year's avoided injuries. No multi-year cohort overlap.
model.counterfactual: Existing GRYD and other partner services, background violence declines, secured funding and activities financed from reserves continue. N is a prospective annual scale, not entirely additional service. a discounts the share that survives without UPI's funding/infrastructure; b separately discounts ordinary private support that replaces reserves or another donor.
model.attribution: Count participant victimizations only, not arrests or all citywide incidents. a=.75 is an explicit, uncertain UPI-enabled fraction of this capacity relative to other partners/funders; no additional credit is taken for the same regrants or coalition-wide decline.
model.uncertainty: Conditional partial best estimate with subjective transport and marginal-funding assumptions. Uncertainty includes no effect and net harm; joint favorable/low-positive scenarios are not probability quantiles. The central is not a recipient-wide measured return.
model.nativeOutcomes: Annual engaged participant-equivalents, fatal and nonfatal shooting victimizations, net avoided deaths and morbidity. Central produces 1.5405 attributed/additional avoided victimizations, including .3081 fatalities, before QALY conversion.

sensitivity: At the central clinical mix of 4.4 QALYs per avoided victimization, $1 million per 10 requires 20.22 net additional avoided victimizations annually; $100,000 per 10 requires 202.22. Central is 1.5405.

With all other central assumptions fixed, the $1 million target needs e=1.3127, exceeding 100%; this participant-only branch cannot reach that target without higher risk, scale, additionality, duration or clinical value. The $100,000 target is still farther away.
Removing all partner and private-funding discounts (a=b=1) improves the central price to about $4.92 million per 10; this is not the default.
Counting two years of equally effective risk reduction per cohort halves price but requires demonstrated durability and careful avoidance of repeated-cohort double counting.
Setting nonfatal health loss to zero worsens central price by 10%; mortality assumptions dominate.
Using the three-year mean expense gives about $8.59 million per 10. Rapid recipient growth makes the latest annual scope the central denominator.

what: PLC provides free civil legal aid across housing, family, immigration, consumer, health and other matters in Orange County.
Its medical-legal partnerships include HIV-related legal help and hospital-based clinics, but ordinary support is not restricted to those services.
A conditional legal-health estimate now uses explicit case-mix, resolution and finite health assumptions at full recipient resource cost; it is not a complete portfolio return.
strengths: Clinical partners offer a concrete route to people with treatment and social barriers.
Original accounts make donated legal resources and ordinary expenditures separately inspectable.

sections.what:
Public Law Center, EIN 95-3709253, is an Orange County pro bono legal-aid recipient. Ordinary support covers direct representation, advice, clinics, nonprofit assistance and impact litigation across many practice areas. Its current homepage reports nearly 3,800 cases and over 75,000 staff/volunteer hours in an unspecified 'last year'; these are approximate scale indicators, not a dated clinical cohort. [Recipient scope](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/)

The AIDS Legal Assistance Project addresses insurance disputes, housing, employment, privacy and estate/family matters for low-income people living with HIV. Not all such work changes medication adherence or survival. [ALAP](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/hiv-aids-legal-assistance/)

Current MLPs include Orange County Health Care Agency, biweekly Hoag clinics and weekly South Orange County family-resource-center clinics. The Health Law Unit handles coverage eligibility, denied services/drugs/equipment, medical review and billing. [Partnerships](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/medical-legal-partnerships/) [Health law](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/health-law/)
sections.monitoring:
The current website describes services and staffing, but the reviewed sources do not provide annual ALAP/health-law unique-client counts, the share initially out of HIV care, coverage retained because of representation, or linked clinical outcomes. A clinic schedule does not identify its patient volume, completed representation or health yield.

Useful monitoring would follow each resolved legal barrier into otherwise-missed treatment, sustained treatment duration, clinical severity, actual household exposure and health change. Legal success without changed care remains a legal outcome; a successful insurance appeal is not automatically the lifetime benefit of treatment. Compare with the help the patient would receive from case managers, hospital advocates, other lawyers and existing programs.

The official-linked volunteer list demonstrates live demand for representation across several legal specialties. It is evidence of potential volunteer matching work, not an audited cash funding gap or an estimate of additional health cases. No private client narrative or identifying detail is reproduced. [Volunteer opportunities](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/case-list/)
sections.qualitative:
A Philadelphia feasibility study randomized two service organizations, enrolling 202 people with HIV. The intervention site had higher odds of viral suppression at three months (OR 2.42, 95% CI 1.06–5.49); the six-month estimate was not significant. With only one site in each arm, site-specific care and implementation differences cannot be confidently separated from the intervention. This is encouraging mechanism evidence, not a portable PLC risk reduction or a lifetime treatment effect. [Original study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10461-025-04901-w)

An individually randomized primary-care MLP trial found lower stress and fewer emergency visits but higher anxiety and hospital use. Some additional hospital use may represent appropriate access, rather than harm; nonetheless, the mixed outcomes do not justify a universally positive QALY-per-legal-case assumption. [Original randomized trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37028914/)

The START antiretroviral trial establishes a real clinical bridge when treatment actually changes: among initially healthy adults with CD4 counts above 500, serious AIDS/non-AIDS events or death occurred at 1.38 versus 0.60 per 100 person-years with deferred versus immediate treatment. That 0.0078 event-per-person-year difference is not a PLC effect. Current patients, interruption duration, event mix and treatment alternatives may differ substantially. It can anchor a conditional clinical calculation, not establish the local strategy-equivalent exposure produced by legal aid. ART was used during 94% of immediate-arm versus 28% of deferred-arm follow-up, so this difference cannot be multiplied directly by additional ART-years. [Original START paper](https://www.natap.org/2015/IAS/nejmoa15068161.pdf)

Housing stability, safety from abuse, reduced financial distress and equitable legal access may generate substantial benefits outside this HIV branch. Conversely, litigation stress, privacy risks, delay and opportunity costs matter. None is silently assigned zero in a claimed complete portfolio return.

The new central scenario is broader than HIV treatment alone: 25% of the approximate 3,800 annual cases are assumed to involve a potentially material health barrier, including access to care, safe housing or personal safety. The current health-law scope and volunteer case list make these mechanisms plausible, but do not establish that percentage. Of those cases, a 25% incremental implemented-resolution probability is assumed relative to hospital advocates, other lawyers and existing protection. A further 25% funding response discounts grants, reserves and volunteer replacement. These are explicit subjective priors, not observed PLC rates.

A changed case receives a net 0.03 annual survival-adjusted utility gain for two years, then zero. This small finite health area is a judgment about heterogeneous clinical, safety and stress effects, not an effect imported from START or the MLP trials. A 10% deduplication/overlap reduction prevents treating repeated legal matters and shared health improvements as fully independent. One affected person's trajectory per case is counted; no automatic family-size or lifetime multiplier is used. Zero and harm remain plausible. Legal and systemic value outside this health-relevant component is unpriced.
sections.cost:
Full recognized resource expense is $21,372,374 in 2024: audited expense of $21,201,323 plus $171,051 of direct event costs netted against revenue. This includes $12,509,436 of donated legal services. The comparable totals are $19,002,911 in 2023 and $13,652,011 in 2022; the three-year mean is $18,009,099. These are not cash-only fundraising needs. [2024 audit](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/2024_Public-Law-Center-Financial-Statements.pdf) [2023 comparative audit](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Public-Law-Center-Financial-Statements-2023.pdf)

For a non-donated accrual-expense spending view, original returns give $8,691,886+$171,051=$8,862,937 in 2024, $7,293,144+$149,786=$7,442,930 in 2023 and $5,706,142+$150,079=$5,856,221 in 2022. The mean is $7,387,363. The 2024 audit-minus-donated-services comparison differs by $1. Donated legal time is a real resource but neither a cash bill nor evidence of health impact; its accounting valuation should not be confused with the much larger promotional valuation of all legal work. [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953709253/202543189349307004/full) [2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953709253/202413199349306851/full) [2022](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953709253/202343189349319484/full)

At full resource cost, $1 million per 10 LA QALYs requires 213.72 net additional QALYs annually; $100,000 requires 2,137.24. Spread across the approximate 3,800 total cases, that is 0.0562 or 0.5624 net QALY per case, after all counterfactual adjustments. This is a required average, not an estimate that every case is a health case. The non-donated accrual-expense view requires 88.63 or 886.29 QALYs instead.

In a clinical illustration only, applying START's 0.0078 event reduction per randomized-strategy follow-up year and assigning five QALYs per avoided composite event gives 0.039 QALY per full-equivalent START-like strategy-year. The five-QALY value is a subjective illustration, not a measured mean. Meeting the full-resource $1 million target would require about 5,480 full-equivalent START-like strategy-years after funding and attribution discounts. This shows why modest short-term viral-suppression acceleration alone cannot establish an attractive recipient-wide return.

Under those stated priors, the full-resource conditional price is about $69.67 million per 10 LA QALYs: 3.06753 net modeled QALYs against $21,372,374 annual cost. Positive joint stress cases range from about $883,717 to $73.56 billion per 10, not confidence limits. Excluding donated legal services changes the central price to approximately $28.89 million per 10 without changing health; that is a different cost perspective, not the preferred full-resource result.
sections.funding:
The latest audit reports $3.11 million in cash and investments and $3.75 million in financial assets available for general expenditure within one year. It restates prior-year legal-settlement revenue by $970,624 and reports a $1.76 million 2024 decline in net assets. This suggests financial pressure but is not a current marginal work plan. The unmodified audit opinion includes an emphasis on that revenue correction. [Audit and liquidity note](https://www.publiclawcenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/2024_Public-Law-Center-Financial-Statements.pdf)

A May 2026 Cornell announcement describes an accepted two-year Equal Justice Works fellowship joining PLC and Emilio Nares Foundation to serve families of children with cancer and other serious illnesses. This is a concrete emerging clinical partnership; fellowship support is already part of the counterfactual, and its announcement does not supply patient volume or an unfunded expansion tranche. [Fellowship](https://www.lawschool.cornell.edu/news/in-the-public-interest-caroline-carrie-atikian-omalley-26/)

The official-linked donation form identifies PLC and offers General Support alongside restricted alternatives. This report evaluates ordinary general support. The next useful diligence is a recipient-level allocation and staffing plan, volunteer conversion capacity, replacement grants and a health-case outcome sample. Existing hospital, public and volunteer resources should be preserved in the counterfactual rather than counted as wholly purchased by a new gift. [Donation route](https://publiclawcenter.networkforgood.com/projects/20106-public-law-center-donations)

what: Inner City Law Center combines eviction defense with benefits access, housing-condition litigation and policy advocacy in Los Angeles.
Its legal services can protect housing and income for people facing serious disadvantage.
The numerical scenario below prices only the short-term health contribution of eviction prevention against recipient-wide costs; it is not a complete portfolio valuation.
strengths: A concrete route connects legal representation to housing stability, with some randomized evidence that representation changes possession outcomes.
The recipient reports completed cases and housing outcomes, not only consultations.
Public-benefits and systemic work may deliver important benefits beyond the priced housing component.
reservations: Reported evictions prevented are not a comparison with what would have happened without assistance.
Current public right-to-counsel funding and other legal-aid providers may replace part of a new gift.
Health utility, marginal funding response and donated-resource accounting remain judgmental or unreconciled.

sections.what: ICLC provides tenant defense, benefits assistance, housing-condition litigation and systemic advocacy. The [current program description](https://innercitylaw.org/what-we-do/) places these services within a broader anti-homelessness portfolio, not an eviction-only charity. Current clinics and 2026 activity establish continuing operations.
sections.monitoring: The [2024 impact report](https://innercitylaw.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/2024-ICLC-Impact-Report.pdf) records 875 evictions prevented, 1,589 cases closed and 3,403 people served. These categories overlap and are not added. It does not establish unique counterfactual evictions averted or sustained health effects. The most useful next evidence would link distinct cases to housing and health at six and twelve months, alongside a comparable untreated or differently served group.
sections.qualitative: The [District Court randomized trial](https://harvardlawreview.org/print/vol-126/the-limits-of-unbundled-legal-assistance-a-randomized-study-in-a-massachusetts-district-court-and-prospects-for-the-future/) found substantially better possession outcomes from full representation than limited assistance in a selected setting. The companion [Housing Court experiment](https://www.povertyactionlab.org/sites/default/files/research-paper/3826_Legal%20assistance%20programs%20Mar2012.pdf) found no significant advantage, supporting a genuine zero case. Separately, [judge-assignment research](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10772599/) connects eviction to subsequent housing instability and hospital use; it does not supply a QALY conversion. Benefits recovery, better housing conditions and policy work are important but unpriced here.
sections.cost: The original returns imply gross Form 990 accrual expenses of $17,090,749 in 2022, $18,745,042 in 2023 and $20,403,467 in 2024, including separately netted event costs. Their mean is $18,746,419. The central resource denominator adds the report’s $12,354,422 donated-service valuation to 2024 Form 990 expenses, reaching $32,757,889. This reconstruction exceeds the impact report’s total by $146,191 and is not a verified audit reconciliation. The conditional housing-health price is about $131.2 million per ten LA QALYs; sensitivity excluding donated legal services is $81.7 million. Neither number values the full portfolio, and neither supports ranking ICLC as though its other work had zero value.
sections.funding: A general gift can sustain staff, coordination and cases not completely financed by contracts. The [original 2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/953697572/202513169349303841/full) reports positive annual net income and substantial net assets; those balances do not establish unrestricted cash available for every program. Current [public-funding advocacy](https://innercitylaw.org/) and already adopted tenant protections belong in the baseline. We assume only half of annual activity-equivalent funding translates into additional services after financing substitution, with zero retained as a plausible outcome. No verified immediate funding gap or extra-case commitment was found.
